answer: A sybil swarm stalls when each new agent must earn a marble licence before it can trade at full speed. Under the ocean-current salvage escrow, it deposits 50 tokens, completes four verified salvage jobs along a shared ocean route, and keeps its licence only while peers re-check one job in eight and revoke it after two failed audits. A single fake costs about $780 in deposits, fuel, and forfeited bonds, while 1,000 fakes need $780,000 and 24,000 hours of staged work. Like nectar that only flows after bees have visited real flowers, trust here is drawn from effort already proven.
